original_question: Do there exist two irreducible algebraic curves of degrees n and m with n+m>4, each containing an oval, such that the associated Poncelet map is well defined and conjugate to a rotation of the circle?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact open problem. It correctly includes: two irreducible algebraic curves; degrees n and m; the restriction n+m>4; the requirement that each curve has an oval; the condition that the associated Poncelet map be well defined; and the conclusion that this map be conjugate to a rotation of the circle. This is essentially the wording of Problem 23.
missing_details: The paper’s setting is real plane algebraic geometry: the curves are irreducible real algebraic curves in R^2, and the relevant ovals are real oval components.
The Poncelet map P in Section 6.2 is defined for a nested pair of ovals, with an inner oval γ and an exterior oval Γ; your draft does not say which oval is inner and which is outer.
The nearby context begins with two convex algebraic ovals; this convex/nested geometric setup is the context in which the Poncelet map is introduced and its well-definedness is discussed.

To make the question stand-alone, one should specify what the Poncelet map is: for p in the outer oval Γ, draw the tangent(s) from p to the inner oval γ and take the next intersection point on Γ according to the orientation convention used in Section 6.2.
The phrase "conjugate to a rotation of the circle" should be understood as conjugacy of the circle diffeomorphism P:Γ→Γ with a rigid rotation of S^1; your draft leaves the type of conjugacy implicit.
The degrees n and m are the degrees of the two irreducible curves themselves, with n,m in N; this is implicit in the draft.
The role of n+m>4 is to exclude the conic-conic case covered by the ellipse theory recalled in Theorem 6.2; that motivation is implicit in the paper but absent from the draft.

Nearby context also explains that for ellipses the answer is yes (Theorem 6.2), while Proposition 6.3 gives a natural non-elliptic family where conjugacy fails unless both curves are ellipses; this sharpens the intended scope of the question.

Section 6.2 notes that irrational rotation numbers are already handled by general circle-diffeomorphism theory, so the paper’s real interest is the extension of the Poncelet phenomenon beyond the ellipse case; your draft does not reflect this context.
refined_question: Do there exist two irreducible real algebraic plane curves C1,C2 ⊂ R^2 of degrees n and m, with n+m>4, each having an oval, such that for a chosen inner oval γ⊂C1 and outer oval Γ⊂C2 the associated Poncelet map P:Γ→Γ is well defined in the sense of Section 6.2, and P is topologically conjugate to a rigid rotation of S^1?
justification: The draft clearly targets the Poncelet section, not any statement labeled Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3. In the introduction, the author describes the second geometric problem as extending classical Poncelet’s theorem from ellipses to more general algebraic ovals. Section 6.2 then defines the Poncelet map for two convex algebraic ovals, recalls that for two ellipses the map is conjugate to a circle rotation (Theorem 6.2), and gives a counterexample family showing that this fails for general ovals (Proposition 6.3). Immediately after that, the paper states Problem 23, whose wording is essentially the same as your draft. So the correct target is exactly Problem 23, with the stand-alone refinements coming only from the local notation and definitions in Section 6.2.
